solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tarantino screenplay?

parts.note: Quentin Tarantino's films are full of gunfire, so his script would be one about firing guns; really it is the film-industry term for the final camera-ready script

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of script the director of Pulp Fiction writes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a violent director's screenplay is literally full of gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: In film-making this is the final version of a screenplay, with camera directions, used during filming.

clue.text: Having ensnared male, she-devil abandons American to die

indicators.note: having ensnared means the she-devil, once shortened, traps the male piece inside it
abandons tells us the American abbreviation drops out of the she-devil

parts.note: a succubus is a female demon of folklore

explanation.surface: A tale of a demon who catches a man, leaves an American behind, and lets him perish.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing US from SUCCUBUS leaves SUCCUB; 'Having ensnared' then puts M inside it, before the final B.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb can mean to die, as in succumbing to one's injuries.

clue.text: What to do when packing a suit with an obvious pattern

definitions.text: What to do when packing a suit with an obvious pattern

parts.words: What to do when packing a suit with an obvious pattern
parts.note: packing a suit you open a suitcase and shut it again, while a lawsuit whose pattern is obvious is one with a foregone outcome

explanation.surface: Packing advice for travelling with a loudly patterned suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is a lawsuit as well as clothing; 'case' covers both luggage and a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal matter so clear-cut that its result is certain is called this, from a case quickly opened and closed.

clue.text: Nadal's opening tie-break point

indicators.note: break means the word tie is split open and something is placed in the gap

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: opening picks the initial letter of the tennis player's name

explanation.surface: Rafael Nadal serving at the first point of a tennis tie-break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie-break' looks like one tennis term, but 'tie' is the word broken and 'break' the signal to split it with N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine is a sharp prong, the point of a fork or antler.

clue.text: Spot 4×4 reversing near no right turn ahead

indicators.note: ahead places the rearranged letters before the reversed vehicle
turn tells us the shortened word near is rearranged
no tells us the right abbreviation is removed from near

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reversing tells us the off-roader's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: a four-by-four vehicle is an SUV, a sport utility vehicle

explanation.surface: Spotting an off-roader backing up near a no-right-turn sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges NEA into NAE, and 'reversing' turns the 4×4's letters round; 'ahead' sets the first before the second. A 4×4 is a four-wheel-drive car.
explanation.definitionFit: A naevus is a birthmark or mole, a coloured spot on the skin.

clue.text: Fibre producer is kind found in Cornwall or Merseyside primarily

indicators.note: found in means the word for kind sits inside the region's letters

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the SW, the South West of England
ilk means kind or type, as in 'of that ilk'
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the county name

explanation.surface: A regional search for a creature producing fibre, in Cornwall or Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall stands for SW, the region it belongs to; Merseyside is a county round Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva of the silk moth spins its cocoon from silk thread, a natural textile.

clue.text: Engineer nervous about type of bar erected in venue

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters of nervous are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: erected in a down answer means the piece is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a Z-bar, or zed bar, is a steel bar with a Z-shaped section

explanation.surface: An anxious engineer putting up some kind of bar at a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: ZED written upwards by 'erected' gives DEZ, which the anagram of nervous goes 'about': REN-DEZ-VOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendezvous is an arranged meeting place, so a venue.

clue.text: He conjures a report up about Stig concealing identity with personal magnetism

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the other material
up here means stirred up, so the letters of a report are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: concealing means the name hides the identity abbreviation inside it

parts.note: taken as written; the Stig is the anonymous racing driver on TV's Top Gear
ID is short for identity, as on an ID card
it, as in 'she has it', means sex appeal or personal magnetism

explanation.surface: A news report about the masked Top Gear driver, whose identity is hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: A REPORT rearranged by 'up' gives PRE...ATOR, wrapped 'about' STIDIG (ID hidden in STIG) plus IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator is a conjuror or sleight-of-hand magician, someone who performs tricks.

clue.text: Ill-informed but not entirely ill-prepared

indicators.note: not entirely means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: unready means not prepared

explanation.surface: Someone poorly informed, though not quite unprepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Unread describes someone who has not read much, so poorly informed or uneducated.

clue.text: Fermented lees can act as a purgative

indicators.note: fermented suggests agitation and change, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that fermented wine dregs can upset the bowels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a link to the definition but is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A purgative purges or clears the body out, which is what to cleanse means.

clue.text: With billion unaccounted-for, repartee between London banks is light

indicators.note: between means the shortened banter sits inside the two London edge letters
banks are the edges, so the first and last letters of the city are used
unaccounted-for means the billion abbreviation goes missing from the word

parts.note: banter is witty repartee

explanation.surface: A billion missing, quips flying between London's riverbanks: the matter seems light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like the Thames riverbanks but means the city name's two edge letters; 'unaccounted-for' drops the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, a source of light.

clue.text: State-run tea shop even lacks parking

indicators.note: lacks means the parking abbreviation is dropped
even tells us to take the letters in even positions from these words

parts.note: P is the parking symbol on road signs

explanation.surface: A state-run tea shop has no parking.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of RUN TEA SHOP are U, T, A, H, P; drop P to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Injured welder must take part in unorthodox event

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An injured welder obliged to compete in an unusual event.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling in a pit of mud is an unconventional contest, often staged as a spectacle.

clue.text: In foreign fields revolutionary is so stuck in the past

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other
foreign suggests something altered and strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolutionary abroad who is stuck in old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is so' read backwards by 'revolutionary' gives OSSI, which goes 'In' the anagram of fields: F-OSSI-LISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Fossilised figuratively means rigidly old-fashioned, unable to change.

clue.text: Partially disrobed, hoping to philander

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone half undressed, hoping for a fling.
explanation.definitionFit: To bed-hop is to go from one sexual partner to another, a slang synonym for womanising.

clue.text: 'If' poet found in abridged present edition

indicators.note: found in means the poet is placed inside the other letters
abridged means the word present is cut short to its first two letters

parts.note: taken as written before cutting
Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses

explanation.surface: Looking for the poet of 'If' in a shortened current edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If' poet suggests Kipling, but 'If' is the definition and the poet is Ovid.
explanation.definitionFit: Provided works as a conjunction meaning on condition that, the same as if.

clue.text: Bouquet containing pansy, alyssum, freesia and spinach hearts is a ridiculous thing

indicators.note: containing means the wine's aroma holds the other letters

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose, its aroma

indicators.note: hearts are the middle letters of each of the four plant names

explanation.surface: A posy of pansy, alyssum and freesia with spinach in it seems absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles of pansy, alyssum, freesia and spinach are N, S, E, N, held by NOSE; 'Bouquet' is a wine's smell, not flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense is foolish or absurd talk or behaviour.

clue.text: Sticking-point after he said nothing new

indicators.note: after puts the compass point at the end, following the anagram
new means remade, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Reaching a sticking-point in talks once he had nothing new to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticking-point' reads as one phrase, but 'point' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the action of sticking to a surface.

clue.text: Greek dish made with a Spanish chicken

parts.note: pollo is Spanish for chicken

explanation.surface: A recipe for a Greek dish cooked with Spanish chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is slang for a good-looking man; Apollo, the Greek god, was the ideal of male beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god Apollo was the model of handsome youth, a heart-throb or dish.

clue.text: Bouncer appears to be recipient of bribe

definitions.meaning: a rubber cord that makes a jumper spring back up, a bouncer
a bung is a bribe, so its recipient is jokingly the ..., like a payee

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman who seems to be on the take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman, but it means the elastic cord a jumper springs on.
explanation.definitionFit: The elastic rope used in leaping from heights bounces the jumper, and the joke reading is one paid a bung.

clue.text: One to fall for self-aggrandizement

parts.note: one's ego is the self, the 'I'
to trip is to stumble or fall

explanation.surface: A person liable to fall for flattery that inflates the self.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done to boost one's self-importance.

clue.text: Wine bottled up in Bristol, remarkably

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the letters are read upwards, backwards
bottled means the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wine bottled in Bristol, to remarkable effect.
explanation.walkthrough: TOLREM spans 'Bristol, remarkably'; read upwards it gives the grape.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the red wine made from it.

clue.text: Not in form, England's outsiders are second best

parts.note: a batsman not in is out
a form at school is a class

indicators.note: outsiders are the first and last letters of the country name

explanation.surface: An out-of-form England side, its fringe players ranked second best.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outclassed is to be beaten by superior opponents, so to come off second best.

clue.text: Fragrance secreted by hot tottie

indicators.note: secreted by means the letters are tucked away within the words

explanation.surface: Perfume worn by an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto, or attar, is a fragrant oil from flowers, especially attar of roses.

clue.text: Taxman nips attempt to become doctor's assistant

indicators.note: nips means the taxman's letters pinch the attempt between them

parts.note: IR, the Inland Revenue, was Britain's tax authority
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A tax inspector trying to become a doctor's helper.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor is Frankenstein, whose hunchbacked assistant in films is Igor.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor is the stock name of the mad scientist's lab assistant in horror films.

clue.text: Australia is enthralled by tourist playing rugby union

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the tourist

parts.note: the British and Irish Lions are the touring rugby team, so a player is a Lion
A is the international vehicle code for Australia

explanation.surface: Australia captivated by a visiting rugby union player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rugby union' reads as one phrase, but 'union' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a link or close relationship, a coming together.

clue.text: More delicate practice shot has length instead of direction

indicators.note: instead of means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: a sighter is a trial shot in shooting or archery
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Adjusting a practice shot for length rather than aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighter means less heavy, finer or more delicate in touch.

clue.text: Plotter dreaded blunders revealing secret communications site

indicators.note: blunders suggests mistakes, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A conspirator's feared mistakes expose a spy's hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Spies leave messages at a hidden place for collection, never meeting face to face.
